Example: A rural health system planning high-risk pregnancy remote monitoring starts with two OB nurses taking BP cuffs home for a week. They use them daily, figure out where instructions are confusing, where devices are finicky.

Then those nurses work with a dozen expecting moms with hypertension who test devices at home and give feedback.

What they discovered: Patients were confused about WHEN to take readings. Morning? Evening? Before or after eating? The vendor manual assumed patients would know.

They didn't.

Adding "take your reading when you wake up, before breakfast" changed everything.

This is what "design with patients and clinicians" means. Putting real devices in real hands and learning what works.

Small scale = discover problems when they're easy to fix, before distributing to thousands.

Technology is 20% of success. Implementation science is 80%.
